candidate_interpretation: No coherent semantic concept. Activation is tied to the literal opening character(s)/token-0 of the prompt (e.g. a curly single-quote '‘' vs straight apostrophe "'" vs the word "What") rather than to any shared meaning. Every top/mid/low example in both Discovery and Confirmation fires exclusively at token_position 0, and near-identical discretized activation values (312.86, 285.23, 255.16...) recur verbatim across completely unrelated prompts that merely happen to open with the same punctuation/word, across all five domains.
evidence_supporting: Cross-domain spread looks superficially impressive (domain_concentration 1.73, cross_domain_entropy_norm 0.999, fires 230-270 times per domain roughly evenly) and template_diversity lists 242-251 'tier1' families, suggesting broad generalization at first glance.
evidence_contradicting: Every single example across top/mid/low/one_per_template in both subsets fires at token_position=0 only. Activation value is essentially a small fixed set of constants (312.86, 285.23, 255.16, 255.14...) that recur identically for wildly unrelated prompts (Hindi vocabulary questions, DNA replication questions, SCIENCE template boilerplate) whose only shared property is the literal character(s) opening the prompt (e.g. '‘' curly quote vs "'" straight quote vs 'What'). The large 'tier1 family' counts are an artifact of each distinct prompt being its own family, not evidence of conceptual generalization. This is purely a positional/surface-token feature.
domain_dependence: Treated as a cross-domain/general candidate (per primary_stratum 'cross_domain_broadly_distributed'): concentration is low and entropy is near-maximal, but this reflects that the same surface punctuation/opening-word patterns occur across all five domains, not that a semantic concept generalizes across domains.
script_language_dependence: Not a script/language marker in the usual sense — activation is keyed to the specific Unicode opening character/word, which happens to correlate with Hindi's use of curly quotes in this corpus, but it fires identically for English SCIENCE/DNA openers ('What'), so it is not tracking Hindi meaning or Hindi script as a whole.
potential_polysemanticity: Functionally polysemantic in the sense that it bundles several unrelated surface-opening-token patterns (curly-quote Hindi questions, apostrophe Hindi questions, 'What is...' English questions) that share no semantic content, only token identity at position 0.

candidate_interpretation: Fires on tokens within Hindi-domain prompts that engage in explicit meta-linguistic comparison/distinction-making — contrasting two Hindi words, grammatical forms, or pragmatic strategies (tense/aspect pairs, synonym pairs, indirect-speech strategies, presupposition). Concentrated in HINDI (66% of firings) across Grammar/Syntax/Semantics/Pragmatics/Vocabulary subdomains, with a much weaker generic floor in other domains.
evidence_supporting: Top examples span many distinct templates and subdomains, all about comparing/distinguishing Hindi linguistic items (tense vs aspect, synonym pairs, indirect speech, presupposition, idiom meaning). 112-114 confirmed tier1 families (not just 1-2), spanning 92-93 distinct subdomains. Confirmation-subset top examples independently reproduce the same theme (e.g. 'aspect difference', 'postposition choice', 'register of Sahitya/alankar'). Five same_concept_different_template counterexamples (tense, case agreement, relative-clause structure) all fired at 0.6-0.91.
evidence_contradicting: A non-trivial secondary floor (~0.15 activation, well below the ~0.9-1.1 top tier) fires on unrelated DNA/SCIENCE/EMOTIONS/GANDHI content with no comparison/distinction theme (e.g. 'role of post-translational modifications', 'historian examines X'), indicating some contamination/noise floor outside the core Hindi theme. script_language_score rises moderately from discovery (1.77) to confirmation (2.20), a ~24% change (below the 50% divergence threshold but worth noting).
domain_dependence: Treated as domain-specific (HINDI, ~66% concentration is the home-domain pattern): assessed diversity within HINDI — strong, spanning Grammar, Syntax, Semantics, Pragmatics, and Vocabulary subdomains with 112+ distinct template families, not a single recurring template.
script_language_dependence: Meaningful Hindi-script share, but activation does not track script alone: it fires at comparable high magnitude on some Romanized-Hindi prompts (e.g. 'Sahitya mein alankar...') and at near-zero on some Devanagari prompts outside the distinction-making theme, suggesting it tracks the comparison/distinction content more than script per se, though this was not directly tested with same_script_unrelated_semantics counterexamples in this bundle.
potential_polysemanticity: Mild: the strong top-tier signal (linguistic comparison) is cleanly thematic, but the low-magnitude cross-domain floor (DNA/SCIENCE/EMOTIONS content unrelated to comparison) suggests a secondary, weaker non-semantic component layered on top.

candidate_interpretation: A script/transliteration marker: fires on Hindi-language content specifically rendered in Romanized/Latin script (not Devanagari), regardless of topic (pragmatics, grammar, vocabulary, semantics all represented). Within HINDI domain only (~94% of firings).
evidence_supporting: Directly tested and confirmed: same_script_unrelated_semantics counterexamples on Devanagari-script Hindi (e.g. 'उसका स्वर मृदु था', 'दीपावली पर...', 'सभा में सभी...') all fired at exactly 0.0, while Romanized-script counterexamples on unrelated vocabulary topics ('Mausam suhaana tha', 'Usne purani yaadon ko sanjokar rakha') fired at 0.49-0.71. This cleanly discriminates script rather than topic. High script_language_score (13.25 discovery, 12.3 confirmation) consistent with the selection stratum 'script_language_dependence'. 5 same_concept_different_template counterexamples (all Romanized-script pragmatics prompts) fired 0.63-0.76.
evidence_contradicting: None found — the same_script_unrelated_semantics test is the strongest possible evidence here and it behaves exactly as a script marker should (fires on Romanized, not on Devanagari, independent of topic).
domain_dependence: Domain-specific framing applies (home domain HINDI, concentration 2.42 expected and not penalized): within HINDI, fires across Pragmatics/Grammar/Syntax/Semantics/Vocabulary subdomains (31-32 subdomains, 24-30 tier1 families), i.e. good internal diversity — but this diversity is topic-diversity riding on a pure script signal, not evidence of a semantic concept.
script_language_dependence: Confirmed to track script/transliteration choice alone, not meaning: fires on any Romanized Hindi content and fails on Devanagari content regardless of topic overlap (directly demonstrated by the same_script_unrelated_semantics counterexamples).
potential_polysemanticity: Not polysemantic — single coherent (non-semantic) trigger: Latin-script rendering of Hindi.

candidate_interpretation: No defensible coherent hypothesis. Extremely rare (123 firing tokens discovery, 118 confirmation; token-level frequency 0.0025), scattered across unrelated domains/subdomains (SCIENCE Environmental science/Astrophysics, DNA Inheritance, GANDHI Methods-of-protest, HINDI Pragmatics, EMOTIONS communication) with no consistent shared theme, and activation is inconsistent even within identical carrier templates.
evidence_supporting: Fires broadly across all five domains (cross_domain_entropy_norm 0.96-0.99), which could superficially suggest a general cross-domain concept, and n meets the minimum-evidence threshold in Confirmation (118 tokens, 92 prompts).
evidence_contradicting: Within the identical SCIENCE carrier template ('How could knowledge of X be applied to reduce or manage...'), activation is wildly inconsistent: fires at 0.035 for 'Analytical chemistry' but exactly 0.0 for 'Materials science', 'Planetary science', and 'Astrophysics' — i.e., the same_concept_different_template counterexamples mostly failed to fire (4 of 5 at 0.0). Template diversity is thin and mostly Tier-3 (12-19 tier1 families vs 72-79 unclustered Tier-3 prompts). Top examples share no discernible common meaning (chi-square genetics test, Gandhi historical methods, Hindi pragmatics, emotional communication, astrophysics) beyond vague 'reasoning/comparison' task framing, which is too generic to call a concept.
domain_dependence: Treated as cross-domain/general per selection stratum: concentration is low but this reflects scattered, inconsistent low-magnitude firing rather than a reproducible cross-domain concept.
script_language_dependence: Not script/language dependent; firing is in both HINDI and English-language domains with no clear script pattern.
potential_polysemanticity: Likely polysemantic/noise — the firing examples do not cohere into even a loose shared theme.

candidate_interpretation: A lexical/topic-name marker for astronomy- and sky-science-adjacent SCIENCE subdomain labels: fires very strongly (1.5-2.0) whenever the literal subdomain name 'Astrophysics' appears in a prompt (regardless of carrier template), and more weakly (0.2-0.3) for semantically adjacent subdomain names 'Atmospheric science' and 'Planetary science'. A much weaker, likely unrelated floor (~0.05-0.3) fires occasionally in other domains.
evidence_supporting: Directly tested: same_concept_different_template counterexamples confirm the pattern cleanly — fires at 2.02 for an 'Astrophysics' prompt but at exactly 0.0 for otherwise-identical carrier templates substituting 'Organic chemistry', 'Physiology', 'Climate science', or 'Chemical kinetics'. Generalizes across >10 distinct SCIENCE carrier-sentence templates (43-50 tier1 families) as long as the subdomain word is Astrophysics/Atmospheric/Planetary science, i.e. it is carrier-template-independent.
evidence_contradicting: A non-trivial lower-magnitude floor (0.05-0.3) fires on semantically unrelated EMOTIONS, DNA, GANDHI, and HINDI content (metaphors for emotion, pyrophosphate release, historical comparisons, indirect speech) with no shared theme to the core astro/sky-science signal — this is likely noise/contamination rather than a second coherent sense.
domain_dependence: Treated as domain-specific to SCIENCE subdomain-naming (the 'cross_domain_broadly_distributed' selection label is misleading here — the real signal is topic-word-specific within SCIENCE): within SCIENCE, diversity is good since it survives across 10+ distinct carrier sentence templates, not one recurring template.
potential_polysemanticity: Mildly polysemantic: a strong, clean lexical-topic sense (Astrophysics/Atmospheric/Planetary science) plus a much weaker, likely unrelated low-magnitude floor in unrelated domains.

candidate_interpretation: A theory-of-mind / empathic-reasoning feature: fires strongly and consistently on the 'Task:' clause of EMOTIONS 'Scenario: ... Task: [interpret/reason about/compare perspectives on] ... Do not infer a person's internal state with certainty...' templates, i.e. prompts that ask the model to reason about another person's emotional state from ambiguous social cues while holding uncertainty.
evidence_supporting: Top-tier activation (1.8-2.0) generalizes cleanly across 5+ distinct Task-clause templates (Identify a relevant concept..., Interpret the social and emotional context..., Reason about plausible perspectives..., Compare two possible interpretations..., Propose a respectful response...) all sharing the empathy/uncertainty theme and the same boilerplate caveat. All 5 same_concept_different_template counterexamples fired at 1.79-1.83, confirming generalization in the independent Confirmation subset. 34-37 tier1 confirmed families (not just 1-2).
evidence_contradicting: A secondary floor (~0.06) fires on HINDI syntax/pragmatics and DNA/SCIENCE content with no empathy theme, suggesting a minor non-semantic contamination at much lower magnitude than the core signal (not a serious threat to the main interpretation).
domain_dependence: Treated as domain-specific (home domain EMOTIONS, 48% of firings, concentration 2.92 expected and not penalized): within EMOTIONS, diversity is strong — Empathy_Social_Emotions and Basic_Complex_Emotions subdomains, 34-37 distinct templates, not one recurring template.
script_language_dependence: Not script/language dependent; the weak HINDI floor firing is at far lower magnitude than the core EMOTIONS signal and unrelated in theme.
potential_polysemanticity: Mostly monosemantic for the empathy/theory-of-mind concept at high activation; the low-magnitude cross-domain floor is a minor, likely separate noise component.

candidate_interpretation: No coherent semantic concept defensible. Fires mostly at very early token positions (1-9) across wildly heterogeneous templates and domains (HINDI syntax/vocabulary/pragmatics, GANDHI 'Place X within ethical argument', SCIENCE 'Researchers encounter...', EMOTIONS 'Distinguish X from Y') with no shared theme beyond early sentence position. This candidate was explicitly drawn from the 'cross_seed_prescreened_nonreproducible_control' stratum, i.e. flagged in advance as a negative control expected to fail cross-seed replication.
evidence_supporting: High frequency and broad template coverage (88 tier1 families) could superficially look like strong generalization.
evidence_contradicting: Top/mid/low examples share no semantic theme — Hindi causative/mood syntax, compound-word vocabulary, politeness pragmatics, Gandhi historical-method prompts, and science-instrumentation prompts are grouped only by firing at token positions 1-9. This is consistent with the preregistered expectation for this stratum (prelim_cross_seed_pass_discovery_only: false), i.e. it is a known-likely-nonreproducible control candidate, not a validated discovery.
domain_dependence: Treated as cross-domain (concentration moderate at 1.82-1.92, mostly HINDI at ~70% but spread across all domains): the cross-domain spread reflects generic early-sentence-structure firing, not a reproducible concept.
script_language_dependence: Elevated script_language_score (3.2-3.4) reflects the HINDI-majority firing share, but activation does not appear to track Hindi meaning — it fires on early tokens regardless of content.
potential_polysemanticity: Effectively a grab-bag of unrelated early-sentence openers; not a single concept.

candidate_interpretation: Primarily a fixed-template detector: produces an almost perfectly constant activation (2.1254) at token_position=2 specifically for the recurring GANDHI carrier sentence 'A historian examines <TOPIC> through political context/documentary evidence. What contextual factors are essential to a careful explanation?', regardless of which of 200+ Gandhi subdomain topics is substituted. A much lower, broadly distributed floor (~0.1) fires across all domains at scattered positions with no clear shared theme.
evidence_supporting: The top-tier activation is essentially invariant (2.1254 repeated to 6 decimal places) across every one of 200+ distinct Gandhi subdomain substitutions, and all 5 same_concept_different_template counterexamples (Sanitation, Ahimsa, England and legal study, Khilafat alliance, Transvaal registration laws) fired at exactly the same value — strong evidence the feature is locked to the literal carrier-sentence wording (likely the word 'examines' or the phrase structure at position 2), not the substituted topic.
evidence_contradicting: Despite being the single highest-frequency candidate reviewed (16% token-level frequency, 83% of prompts), the enormous 'tier1_confirmed_families' count (202-203) is an artifact of each distinct topic substitution being clustered as its own 'family' even though they share one carrier sentence — it does not indicate 202 independent semantic generalizations. The broad low-magnitude floor (~0.1) across HINDI/EMOTIONS/SCIENCE/DNA content shares no discernible theme with the Gandhi-historian signal.
domain_dependence: Treated as cross-domain per selection stratum ('high_frequency'), but the dominant top-tier signal is GANDHI-template-specific, not a generalizing cross-domain concept; the broad low floor elsewhere is noise rather than evidence of real cross-domain concentration.
script_language_dependence: Not meaningfully script/language dependent despite moderate script_language_score; the low floor spans both Hindi-script and English-language domains without a clear pattern.
potential_polysemanticity: Two components: (1) a template-locked spike for one specific Gandhi carrier sentence, and (2) an unrelated low-magnitude broadly-distributed floor — these do not share a common concept.

candidate_interpretation: A broad Hindi/Devanagari-script detector that fires at mid-to-late token positions across almost any Hindi-language content, with somewhat higher magnitude on explicit grammatical/semantic-analysis prompts (tense/aspect, case marking, figurative meaning) than on pragmatics/scenario prompts. Explicitly drawn from the 'cross_seed_prescreened_nonreproducible_control' stratum (a deliberate negative control expected to fail cross-seed replication).
evidence_supporting: Strongly concentrated in HINDI (85% of firings), consistent script_language_score (2.3-2.4) across Discovery/Confirmation. All 5 same_concept_different_template counterexamples (tense/aspect distinctions) fired at 0.18-0.56.
evidence_contradicting: Critically, all 5 same_script_unrelated_semantics counterexamples (Hindi pragmatics scenarios about presupposition, turn-taking, social distance — topics unrelated to the apparent grammar/case-marking theme) also fired, just at lower magnitude (0.017-0.145) — i.e. the feature does not cleanly discriminate 'on-theme' from 'off-theme' same-script content, it just fires more weakly on it. This is consistent with a generic script/length-dependent floor rather than a clean semantic concept, and matches the preregistered expectation that this candidate is a nonreproducible control.
domain_dependence: Treated as domain-specific (HINDI, concentration 2.2 expected): some internal gradation by theme exists (grammar/case-marking prompts activate higher than pragmatics scenarios) but the gradation is weak and the feature fires broadly regardless.
script_language_dependence: Appears to track Hindi/Devanagari script broadly rather than cleanly tracking meaning — it fires (at reduced but nonzero magnitude) even on same-script content outside its apparent grammar-analysis theme.
potential_polysemanticity: Likely a single script-driven mechanism with a magnitude gradient rather than two distinct senses.

candidate_interpretation: A Hindi grammatical/case-marking meta-linguistic analysis feature: fires at late token positions (49-153, i.e. near the end of longer analytical questions) on Hindi prompts specifically discussing case markers (karak/parsarg), postpositions, verb-agreement, and tense/aspect distinctions. Heavily concentrated in HINDI (~90%).
evidence_supporting: Top examples consistently involve explicit grammatical analysis (postposition 'ko' vs 'ne', closest-conjunct agreement, case-marked vs unmarked objects, tense/aspect contrasts) across 46-48 distinct tier1 template families and 49-73 subdomains. 5 of 5 same_concept_different_template counterexamples (auxiliary-verb order, correlative constructions, tense/aspect) fired at 0.26-0.53.
evidence_contradicting: same_script_unrelated_semantics counterexamples (e.g. plain verb-meaning questions) also fired, but at much lower magnitude (~0.05) — showing partial, not clean, discrimination between on-theme grammatical-analysis content and generic Hindi content. Low cross_domain_entropy_norm (0.28) and high domain concentration (2.34-2.42) indicate this is essentially single-domain.
domain_dependence: Treated as domain-specific (home domain HINDI, concentration 2.34-2.42 expected and not penalized): diversity within HINDI is moderate — 46-48 tier1 families across Grammar/Syntax/Pragmatics/Vocabulary, though a large share (274-310) remains Tier-3 unclustered.
script_language_dependence: Partially meaning-tracking: activates more for explicit case/tense-marking analysis than for generic same-script vocabulary content, but the gap (0.3-0.56 vs ~0.05) suggests a real but weak theme-dependent gradient layered on a broad script-sensitive base rate.
potential_polysemanticity: Likely a single grammatical-analysis sense with a magnitude gradient by topical relevance, rather than multiple unrelated senses.

candidate_interpretation: An indirect-speech-act / pragmatic-intent detector: fires on Hindi prompts presenting a quoted utterance in a social scenario (parent-child, teacher-student, workplace) followed by a question about the speaker's real/indirect/practical intent or implied meaning, as distinct from the literal words.
evidence_supporting: Top examples are thematically tight: quoted dialogue + 'what is the real/indirect/practical purpose of this statement' across varied social settings (mother-son, teacher-student, manager-employee, friend-to-friend). Directly confirmed by counterexamples: 3 of 5 same_concept_different_template examples (new quoted-dialogue + intent question) fired strongly (1.08, 1.07, 0.54) in the independent Confirmation subset, while all 5 same_script_unrelated_semantics counterexamples (plain Hindi vocabulary/adjective-meaning questions with no implied-intent framing) fired at exactly 0.0 — a clean positive/negative discrimination that rules out a pure script-marker explanation.
evidence_contradicting: Two same_concept_different_template counterexamples (grammar-focused: subjunctive mood choice, causative-verb entailment) fired at 0.0 despite superficially resembling the pattern, indicating the feature requires the quoted-dialogue + implied-intent framing specifically, not just any pragmatics-adjacent Hindi sentence. Template diversity is thin (only 11 tier1 confirmed families in Confirmation, heavily Tier-3 at 120/166 unclustered).
domain_dependence: Treated as domain-specific (home domain HINDI at ~85-93%, with some EMOTIONS overlap): diversity within HINDI covers Pragmatics, Semantics, and some Vocabulary subdomains, consistent with a real sub-concept of Hindi pragmatics rather than one repeated template, though confirmed-family count is modest.
script_language_dependence: Clearly tracks meaning, not script alone: the direct same_script_unrelated_semantics test shows it fails to fire on unrelated same-script (Devanagari) vocabulary content, ruling out a pure script-marker story.
potential_polysemanticity: Appears monosemantic — one coherent pragmatic concept (quoted-utterance + implied-intent framing).

candidate_interpretation: A cross-domain pragmatic/communicative-intent-inference feature: fires on prompts (in both HINDI Pragmatics and EMOTIONS Emotional_Recognition/Expression_Communication subdomains) that ask the model to infer a speaker's/communicator's underlying intent, ambiguity, or implied meaning behind an utterance or message, independent of language.
evidence_supporting: Top-tier activation (0.5-0.66) spans both HINDI Pragmatics (deixis 'yahan/vahan', literal-vs-context-based reference) and is echoed by Confirmation counterexamples in both HINDI Pragmatics (5 same_concept_different_template examples, 0.19-0.38, all fired) and EMOTIONS (3 different_domain_same_surface_form examples about ambiguous messages/emotional intent, 0.03-0.40, fired) — i.e. the concept generalizes across the two domains where 'inferring communicative intent' is a natural fit. 126-128 tier1 confirmed families.
evidence_contradicting: A handful of top examples (DNA ribosome stalling, GANDHI classroom-activity design) do not fit the pragmatic-intent theme and activate at similarly high magnitude (0.55-0.59), which is a real unresolved tension; a secondary low floor (~0.09) also fires broadly on unrelated DNA/GANDHI/SCIENCE content.
domain_dependence: Treated as a cross-domain/general candidate (moderate concentration 1.70-1.71, cross_domain_entropy 0.67-0.69): partial support — the HINDI+EMOTIONS pragmatic-intent concentration (HINDI 1449/2194 + EMOTIONS 215/2194 ≈ 76%) is plausible and thematically coherent, but the residual DNA/GANDHI/SCIENCE firings (24%) are not explained by the same concept, weakening a clean cross-domain story.
script_language_dependence: Not purely script-dependent: fires at comparable high magnitude in both Hindi-script Pragmatics prompts and English-language EMOTIONS prompts, supporting a meaning-based (not script-based) mechanism for the core signal.
potential_polysemanticity: Likely polysemantic: a core pragmatic-intent-inference sense (HINDI Pragmatics + EMOTIONS communication) plus an unexplained secondary component firing on unrelated DNA/GANDHI/SCIENCE content at similar or lower magnitude.

candidate_interpretation: No defensible hypothesis. This candidate fires on exactly 1 token in Discovery and exactly 1 token in Confirmation (different prompts each time), both at token_position 0 of short Hindi/English-mixed prompts about public-notice phrases ('Entry by appointment only', 'Please keep the aisle clear'). All 6 counterexamples failed to fire (0.0).
evidence_supporting: None meaningful — the two firing examples share a loose surface similarity (both are public-notice/instruction phrases in quotes at the start of a Hindi-translation prompt), but n=1 per subset is far too thin to support any claim, and confirmation_meets_minimum_evidence_rule is explicitly false.
evidence_contradicting: All 6 targeted counterexamples (including other public-notice/instruction-style Hindi prompts) fired at exactly 0.0, directly undermining even the loose 'public notice phrase' guess. Confirmation evidence is below the minimum threshold (1 firing token, 1 unique prompt).
domain_dependence: N/A — insufficient data to assess either cross-domain or within-domain diversity (only 1 domain, 1 prompt, 1 subdomain observed in each subset).
script_language_dependence: N/A — insufficient firing data; script_language_score is reported as 0.0.

candidate_interpretation: No defensible hypothesis. Fires on exactly 1 token in Discovery (a Hindi prompt about address-register differences, 'Behen ji' vs 'Madam') and on zero tokens in the entire Confirmation subset — the feature failed to replicate at all on independent data.
evidence_supporting: None — there is no Confirmation-subset evidence of any kind to support or refute an interpretation.
evidence_contradicting: Complete failure to fire in Confirmation (0 firing tokens, 0 unique prompts); all 11 counterexamples, including a near-duplicate of the one Discovery example ('Kisi anjan mahila ko Behen ji kehne aur Madam kehne...'), fired at exactly 0.0. confirmation_meets_minimum_evidence_rule is false, and the lack of any Confirmation firing is itself strong evidence against this being a real, reproducible feature.
domain_dependence: N/A — insufficient data (n=1 discovery, n=0 confirmation).
script_language_dependence: N/A — insufficient data; the single firing example is Romanized Hindi but this cannot be generalized from n=1 with zero replication.
potential_polysemanticity: Cannot be assessed with n=1 and zero replication.
